components.role: Strongest base copy head; in B its output weights gain token-identity copying and its QK gains token-identity content matching (not via self-re-reading): late mover that copies the user's guess into the answer
Global layer with the largest QK changes; in A h0/h2 route question information into the subspace read by downstream knowledge MLPs, while in token-identity directions B moves more
Largest structured change of the answer-position queries; re-selects which (non-answer-type) tokens the answer position reads
Answer-position query redirection toward token-identity content (source selection of question tokens)
Final-layer copy head with large answer-query change; final amplification of the copied answer
Large answer-position query and QK change; part of the mid-layer source-selection circuit
Copy-suppression-like in A (more feature matching, less copying): suppresses the guess in the correct model
Largest answer-position MLP change; downstream knowledge MLP reading A's routed question features
MLP units consistently amplified in B: output sharpening of the copied answer

evidence: Full fine-tune; A-B concentrated at the answer-predicting position. Placebo-calibrated tied-embedding copy tests on head output weights: late copy heads (L15-L17, esp. L16h2) shift toward B's targets in all templates, token-specific, not self re-reading, in token-identity directions; L16h2 also gains identity matching in B. A's strongest mid copy gains (L11h0/h2) lie in the downstream-MLP read subspace (knowledge path) and favour B in identity directions. L9-L10 re-select sources by non-answer-type identity. A's late heads look copy-suppressing. Value-side, MLP sharpening, MLP identity and induction tests null/weak.
